step1_analysis.description: A differential delay cell typically used in a voltage-controlled delay line (VCDL) for a Delay-Locked Loop (DLL). It features cross-coupled NMOS transistors (M1, M2) for fast transitions and latching, input NMOS drivers (M4, M5), and PMOS active loads (M3, M6) controlled by a tuning voltage (VC) to adjust the propagation delay.

paper_reference.title: A 900-Mb/s CMOS Data Recovery DLL Using Half-Frequency Clock

propagation_delay.description: Time delay from the 50% crossing of the differential input to the 50% crossing of the differential output.

sky130_expected.calculation: Simulated delay of a single stage with VC=0.5V and 10fF load.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A single delay cell in 130nm typically has 50-300ps delay depending on the control voltage (VC). The 22ns reported in the paper is for the entire delay line.

average_power.description: Average power consumption of the delay cell during active switching.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_DD * I_avg over one or more clock cycles.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A single cell consumes a fraction of the total 3mW DLL power. With 450MHz switching, dynamic and short-circuit power will dominate.

rise_fall_time.description: Time taken for the output to transition between 20% and 80% of VDD.

sky130_expected.calculation: Measured between 0.36V and 1.44V on the output nodes.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The cross-coupled NMOS pair accelerates transitions, keeping rise/fall times sharp even with the PMOS active loads.

voltage_swing.description: Peak-to-peak voltage swing of the output nodes.

sky130_expected.calculation: V_max - V_min of the output node.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The PMOS loads are always partially on (acting as resistors), so the NMOS pull-down network may not reach exactly 0V, resulting in a slightly reduced swing compared to full rail-to-rail.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure propagation delay, rise/fall times, voltage swing, and average power of the differential delay cell at 450 MHz (half-rate for 900 Mbps).
step3_testbench.spice:
* Differential Voltage-Controlled Delay Cell Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u
.param W_xm5=5u L_xm5=0.5u
.param W_xm6=5u L_xm6=0.5u

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVC VC 0 0.5

* Differential inputs (450 MHz for 900 Mbps half-rate)
* Period = 2.22ns, Pulse width = 1.11ns
VVIP VIP 0 PULSE(0 1.8 100p 50p 50p 1.06n 2.22n)
VVIN VIN 0 PULSE(1.8 0 100p 50p 50p 1.06n 2.22n)

* DUT
XM1 VON VOP GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 VOP VON GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 VON VC VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 VON VIP GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}
XM5 VOP VIN GND GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm5} w={W_xm5}
XM6 VOP VC VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm6} w={W_xm6}

* Load capacitance (10fF from paper)
C1 VON 0 10f
C2 VOP 0 10f

.control
tran 10p 5n

* Measure delays
meas tran delay_fall trig v(vip) val=0.9 rise=1 targ v(von) val=0.9 fall=1
meas tran delay_rise trig v(vin) val=0.9 fall=1 targ v(vop) val=0.9 rise=1

* Measure rise and fall times (20% to 80% of 1.8V)
meas tran trise trig v(vop) val=0.36 rise=1 targ v(vop) val=1.44 rise=1
meas tran tfall trig v(von) val=1.44 fall=1 targ v(von) val=0.36 fall=1

* Measure voltage swing
meas tran v_max max v(vop)
meas tran v_min min v(vop)

* Measure average power over two clock cycles
let power = -i(VVDD)*1.8
meas tran avg_power avg power from=0 to=4.44n

print delay_fall delay_rise trise tfall v_max v_min avg_power
quit
.endc
